samples.summary: The rewrite's stated purpose — degrading instead of throwing when `blockParentMap` describes a shape the layout/document no longer has — has no test
samples.evidence: The new comment at text-editor.ts:4062-4069 explicitly justifies making every lookup optional and dropping `doc.getBlock`: "`blockParentMap` can describe a shape the layout or the document no longer has (a remote edit removing rows, a layout computed before the local insertion) ... it must degrade to the block-wide range rather than throw." The old code (`this.doc.getBlock(cellInfo.tableBlockId)`, `tableData!.rows[rowIndex].cells[colIndex]`) would throw in exactly those cases, so this is a real behavior change (crash → block-wide range). Nothing in packages/docs/test/view/cell-hf-wrap-affinity.test.ts constructs a stale layout / stale blockParentMap: all four new tests build a consistent document, mount, and click/type. I grepped the docs test tree for tests exercising getWrapAffinity/getVisualLineRange with a stale layout and found only this file.

samples.summary: Nested-cell coverage is one level deep with a single-block, unmerged cell — the depth/index-sensitive parts of the new lookup are untested
samples.evidence: The new nested test builds exactly one level of nesting (`outer` containing `inner`) with a single paragraph in a single cell, so `cellInfo.rowIndex/colIndex` are always 0, `cbi` is always 0, `blockBoundaries[cbi]` is always 0, and `layoutCell.merged` is always false. The changed code newly indexes `resolved.dataBlock.tableData?.rows[rowIndex]?.cells[colIndex]` and `cell.blocks.findIndex(...)` against the *resolved* nested data block; a wrong dataBlock (e.g. outer instead of inner) would still pass with this fixture whenever the shapes coincide. No test covers cbi > 0 (a cell with several blocks), a non-zero row/col, deeper than one nesting level, or the `!layoutCell.merged` skip, despite the comment claiming correctness "at any nesting depth".

samples.summary: `affinity()` probes `cursor.position.lineAffinity`, not the `cursor.lineAffinity` the feature sets, so it can only ever observe mouse-derived positions
samples.evidence: `_getCursorForTest` returns `{ ...cursor.position }` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3681) and `lineAffinity` on `Cursor` is a separate field (cursor.ts:13). Only the mouse paths put `lineAffinity` *inside* the position object (text-editor.ts:1536, 1593, 1796, 4461...); the typing path calls `cursor.moveTo(newPos, this.getWrapAffinity(newPos))` with a bare `{blockId, offset}` (e.g. text-editor.ts:3647), so `affinity()` would read `undefined` there. The helper therefore asserts a field the mouse handler happened to copy into the position rather than the caret affinity actually used for rendering/End, and it is unusable for the path this delta changes (getWrapAffinity). Not vacuous as written (all `affinity()` assertions follow clicks), but the assertion is indirect and would silently become unobservable if the mouse path stopped copying the field.

samples.summary: No assertion isolates getWrapAffinity's nested-cell result; the nested test would already fail pre-fix at an earlier, unrelated assertion
samples.evidence: In the nested test the only assertion that directly reads affinity comes from the *click* path (line 317), which this delta did not change. The typing path is checked only indirectly via `expectForwardAffinityAtBoundary` (line 323) → End motion. But pre-fix `getVisualLineRange` returned `[0,0]` for a nested cell block (not in `layout.blocks`), so `firstWrapBoundary` at line 311 would already fail its `expect(boundary).toBeGreaterThan(0)` — i.e. the test fails for "End is completely broken in nested cells", not for the wrap-affinity behavior it names. An assertion that observes `cursor.lineAffinity` after typing at the boundary in a nested cell (which the current `affinity()` helper cannot see) would pin the changed behavior directly.

finding.summary: The pixel hit-test affinity changes (the bulk of the diff) have no test that exercises them
finding.evidence: The diff adds `affinityForOffset`/`hitTestLineAffinity` wiring at four hit-test sites: the header/footer line hit-test (~text-editor.ts:4431), the merged-cell resolver (~4546), `resolveOffsetInCellAtPoint` (~4804) and `resolveOffsetInTableAtPoint` (~5003), plus new `lineAffinity` on `CellHitTest` fallbacks. The only new test file, packages/docs/test/view/cell-hf-wrap-affinity.test.ts, exercises (a) the pure helper `hitTestLineAffinity` with three literal-argument calls (lines 74-86) and (b) typing + End, which goes through `getWrapAffinity` (lines 144-187). Nothing dispatches a mouse event: grep for `mousedown|MouseEvent` across packages/docs/test matches only editor-contextmenu.test.ts, and no test references `resolveOffsetInCell`. So if any call site passed the wrong `lineStartOffset` or the wrong `isFirstLineOfBlock` (e.g. `li === 0` vs `li === blockStartLine`), every test in the suite would still pass — the unit tests of the helper cannot detect miswiring.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is false in the working tree. packages/docs/test/view/cell-hf-wrap-affinity.test.ts contains a real mouse-driven hit-test harness: clickAt() dispatches `new MouseEvent('mousedown', {clientX, clientY, ...})` on the editor container (lines 181-192), with a getBoundingClientRect shim added expressly to make the pixel hit-tests reachable (lines 58-65). Three tests then click and assert the affinity the hit-test produced: a wrapped-line start inside a table cell yields offset===boundary + 'forward', one glyph in yields 'backward' (lines 270-295, exercising resolveOffsetInCellAtPoint's affinityForOffset at text-editor.ts:4821-4822/4879/4886); a nested cell yields 'forward' (lines 297-324, reaching the nested/table resolver via text-editor.ts:4868); and a header wrapped-line start yields 'forward' vs 'backward' one glyph in (lines 326-352, exercising getHFPositionFromMouse at text-editor.ts:4447-4466). The assertions are non-vacuous: mousedown stores the hit-test affinity on the cursor position (text-editor.ts:1533-1537, 1605-1611, 1642-1646), DocPosition carries lineAffinity (model/types.ts:213), and editor.ts:3681 spreads cursor.position into _getCursorForTest, so a wrong lineStartOffset at these call sites flips the asserted value. The reviewer's grep claim that only editor-contextmenu.test.ts mentions MouseEvent is contradicted by line 190 of the file they claim to have read in full.
